title: Le Griffon
subtitle: Lake Michigan · 1679
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the upper Great Lakes in autumn 1679, a cold freshwater lake with dark pine shorelines, seventeenth-century French wooden sailing craft, grey-green water under pale overcast light, melancholy and uncanny, vertical 9:16 full-bleed composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no flags, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Lake Michigan, September sixteen seventy-nine. The Griffon, the first full-sized sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, sailed from Washington Island for Niagara.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: a small seventeenth-century French wooden sailing barque, two masts with pale square and fore-and-aft sails set, dark tarred hull with a raised stern, a carved wooden figurehead at the bow, centred in the middle third of the frame and well lit by clear autumn daylight on a grey-green lake, the whole ship sharply legible against the bright water, a low dark pine shoreline far behind, no flags, no lettering, no people.

beats.vo: Her cargo was furs. Six men were aboard: her pilot, and five crew.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: the dim wooden hold of a seventeenth-century sailing ship, bales of beaver pelts tied with rope stacked high in the centre, a single shaft of pale daylight falling through an open hatch onto them, rough oak beams, still and silent, no people.

beats.vo: She never reached Niagara. No one aboard was ever seen again.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: a remote rocky island shore at the edge of a vast grey lake at dusk, an empty sheltered cove with dark pines, calm black water and a pale band of light on the horizon, nothing on the water anywhere, cold and uncanny, no people.

beats.vo: A friar from the expedition blamed a violent storm. La Salle believed his crew sank her, and took the furs. Neither was ever proven.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: a huge autumn storm rolling over a wide freshwater lake, towering dark clouds and steep grey-white waves, wind-driven spray, a faint pale gap of light low on the horizon, no ship, no people.

beats.vo: Wrecks in two lakes have been claimed as hers. None has ever been confirmed. The Griffon has never been found.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: deep under clear cold green lake water, a shaft of pale light falling onto an empty sandy lakebed with a few scattered dark stones, nothing else, silent and unresolved, no people.

facts.claim: Le Griffon, La Salle's barque, built 1679 above Niagara Falls; called the first full-sized sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes
Sailed 18 September 1679 from Washington Island (entrance to Green Bay, Lake Michigan) bound for the Niagara River
Cargo of furs; aboard were the pilot (Luc) and five crew, six in all
Never arrived; considered lost by end of November 1679; neither ship nor crew ever seen again
Hennepin (friar with the expedition) wrote she was lost in a violent storm; La Salle believed the pilot and crew sank her and took the goods; no theory proven

Many wrecks in Lake Michigan and Lake Huron claimed as Le Griffon (incl. Manitoulin 1898, Poverty Island 2001/2013, 2014 bowstem — a tug, 2018); none confirmed; 2022 Michigan state archaeologist: 'The Griffon has not been found'; still unfound July 2026
